failure_analysis.what: Primary score 1468.902 μs/op vs baseline 1336.029 μs/op (+9.94% regression). Changes: (1) cached SessionConfig as private val built once in constructor, (2) collapsed 2-query pattern in connectedComponents/pageRank/detectCyclesViaFallback to single combined MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) RETURN a, b (with conditional isolated-vertex query only when needed).
failure_analysis.why: The measured benchmarks (createVertex, createEdge, findVertexById, findVerticesByLabel, neighbors, shortestPath, allPaths) do NOT exercise connectedComponents/pageRank/detectCyclesViaFallback, so the collapsed-query optimization has zero measurable impact on the primary metric. The SessionConfig caching is a trivial micro-optimization: the original object construction cost (~100ns per session) is negligible compared to Bolt round-trip latency (~100 μs). Variance in AGE+Neo4j benchmarks on local Testcontainers (std dev up to ±2531 μs on neo4j_createVertex) dwarfs any optimization signal, and some benchmarks drifted upward (e.g. neo4j_createEdge 3090.315 vs round-2 baseline territory). The large variance explains the 9.94% swing despite hot-path code remaining effectively identical for benchmarked methods.
failure_analysis.lesson: Round 3 confirms Round 2 lesson: micro-optimizations to Neo4j driver session setup (SessionConfig caching) yield no measurable gain because benchmark primary is dominated by Bolt network I/O + Testcontainers variance. Additionally, collapsing 2-query patterns in algorithm methods (CC, pageRank, cycles) is invisible to this benchmark suite because those methods are not measured. Future rounds must either (a) target a code path that is actually exercised by benchmarks (createVertex, createEdge, findVertexById, shortestPath, allPaths, neighbors, findVerticesByLabel), or (b) expand the benchmark suite to cover algorithm methods before attempting their optimization. High-variance benchmarks (std dev > primary score) make sub-1% gains unmeasurable; only interventions with expected impact >>10% are statistically detectable here.
